source_refs.note: Book p. 270: 14.2.4 properties (i)-(v) of the dot product. Book error: (i) printed as u.v = 0 => u = 0 or v = 0 (false; u perpendicular to v also gives 0). Reasons, checks, tips, mistakes are ours.

blocks.text: Jaise aam numbers ki zarb ke kuch qaide (rules) hote hain, jaise \(ab = ba\) aur \(a(b + c) = ab + ac\), waise hi dot product ke bhi qaide hain. Yeh qaide hisaab ko chhota aur saaf bana dete hain. Lekin ek jagah dot product aam numbers se mukhtalif (different) hai, aur wahi jagah kitab mein bhi ghalat chhap gayi hai. Chaliye dekhte hain.
Farz karein \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) vectors hain aur \(c\) koi bhi real number hai. To:

items: (i) \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0 \iff \underline{u} = \underline{0}\), ya \(\underline{v} = \underline{0}\), ya \(\underline{u} \perp \underline{v}\) (sahi shakal; neeche Kitab ki ghalti dekhiye)
(iv) \((c\underline{u}) \cdot \underline{v} = c(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v})\) (\(c\) scalar hai: number bahar aa jata hai)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab mein property (i) yun chhapi hai: "\(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0 \Rightarrow \underline{u} = \underline{0}\) or \(\underline{v} = \underline{0}\)". Yeh vectors ke liye sahi nahin. Misaal: \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = 0\), halaan ke na \(\underline{i}\) zero vector hai na \(\underline{j}\). Sahi baat yeh hai:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0 \iff \underline{u} = \underline{0} \text{ or } \underline{v} = \underline{0}\]
\[\text{or } \underline{u} \perp \underline{v}\]
Yani agar dono vectors non-zero hon to \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\) ka matlab sirf yeh hai ke woh perpendicular hain (14.2.6).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Numbers mein \(ab = 0\) ho to \(a = 0\) ya \(b = 0\) zaroor hota hai. Dot product mein aisa kyun nahin? Kyun ke \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\) mein teen cheezein multiply ho rahi hain, sirf do nahin. Teesri cheez \(\cos\theta\) bhi zero ho sakti hai, jab \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\). Isi liye perpendicular vectors ka dot product zero hota hai, chahe dono kitne hi lambe hon.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Baqi properties sahi kyun hain? \(\underline{u} = a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k}\) waghaira likh kar component formula (14.2.5) lagayein:
(ii) \(a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2} = a_{2}a_{1} + b_{2}b_{1} + c_{2}c_{1}\). Kyun: aam numbers ki zarb mein tarteeb se farq nahin parta (14.2.2 (c) mein bhi yahi dekha).
(iii) \(\underline{v} + \underline{w}\) ka har component ek jor hai, jaise \(a_{2} + a_{3}\). Phir \(a_{1}(a_{2} + a_{3}) = a_{1}a_{2} + a_{1}a_{3}\), aur baqi components mein bhi yahi. Kyun: numbers ka distributive qaida har component par alag alag lag jata hai.
(iv) \(c\underline{u}\) ke components \(ca_{1}, cb_{1}, cc_{1}\) hain, is liye har term mein \(c\) common hai aur bahar aa jata hai.
(v) Vector ka apne aap se angle \(0\) hai: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{u} = |\underline{u}||\underline{u}|\cos 0 = |\underline{u}|^{2}\). Yeh property magnitude nikalne ka shortcut hai: \(|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{u}}\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice, kitab ka sawal nahin.) Property (iii) ko numbers se check karte hain: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j}\), \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = \underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
Pehle bracket ke andar jama:
\[\underline{v} + \underline{w} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 0\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = 3 + 2 + 0 = 5\]
Ab alag alag:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 3 + 0 + 0 = 3,\quad \underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = 0 + 2 + 0 = 2\]
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} + \underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = 3 + 2 = 5\]
Dono taraf \(5\). Property (v) se: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{u} = 1 + 4 = 5\), is liye \(|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{5}\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = \underline{u} \cdot \underline{w}\) ho, kya hum \(\underline{u}\) "cancel" kar ke \(\underline{v} = \underline{w}\) keh sakte hain? Sochiye, phir parhiye. Jawab: nahin. Misaal: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{j}\), \(\underline{w} = \underline{k}\). Dono dot products zero hain, magar \(\underline{j} \ne \underline{k}\). Hum sirf itna keh sakte hain ke \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} - \underline{w}) = 0\), yani \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v} - \underline{w}\) perpendicular hain (ya \(\underline{u} = \underline{0}\)).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Commutative: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = \underline{v} \cdot \underline{u}\).
2. Distributive: \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = \underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} + \underline{u} \cdot \underline{w}\); brackets algebra ki tarah khulti hain.
3. Scalar bahar aata hai: \((c\underline{u}) \cdot \underline{v} = c(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v})\).
4. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{u} = |\underline{u}|^{2}\).
5. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\) ka matlab zaroori nahin ke koi vector zero ho; perpendicular bhi ho sakte hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\) dekh kar foran keh dena ke ek vector zero hai. Pehle sochiye: kya yeh perpendicular to nahin?
2. Dot product mein vector ko "cancel" karna: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = \underline{u} \cdot \underline{w}\) se \(\underline{v} = \underline{w}\) nahin nikalta.
3. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{u} = |\underline{u}|\) likh dena. Sahi \(|\underline{u}|^{2}\) hai; magnitude ke liye square root lena parta hai.
